subject: Clarify SDK reconnect semantics + demo stabilization plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Chen <ryan@atrialabs.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify SDK reconnect semantics + demo stabilization plan

Ryan / Logan —

Thanks again for pulling off yesterday's demo. A quick follow-up: Ryan mentioned a client-side reconnect behavior that caused duplicate partial responses in the streaming session when network flapped for ~3s. We want to be explicit about what the SDK should guarantee for the POC so Atria doesn't hit this in your production pilot.

Ask: Can the runtime/SDK team confirm the expected semantics on reconnect within an active session (prefetch + KV cache enabled)? Specifically:
- If a client reconnects within 5s, do we restart from the last acknowledged token or request a new generation?
- Any determinism guarantees we can promise for demos (e.g., idempotent reconnect token, retry window)?

Proposed near-term stabilization plan (for our POC demo next week):
1) Short-term: Enable an SDK flag to turn on deterministic reconnect (client sends last-ack token and runtime ties to existing KV cache) — fallback to new generation if mismatch.
2) Runtime: Add a 10s soft-window where reconnect attempts try to reuse the same session id before falling back.
3) Sales/SE: We ship a doc and a sample snippet for Atria to include during their load tests.

Can Logan / Dev weigh in on feasibility today? I can loop engineering contacts into a quick 30-min sync if helpful. Ryan — cc'ing you so you're aligned on the ask; if this is blocking, tell us and we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

---
Attachments: atrialabs-demo-repro-logs.txt (text), demo-stabilization-plan-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ryan Chen <ryan@atrialabs.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify SDK reconnect semantics + demo stabilization plan

Tessa / Ryan —

Thanks for the clear write-up. Short answer: we don't currently expose a single "deterministic reconnect" flag across SDKs; behavior depends on whether the client replays the last ACKed token vs. issuing a fresh request. That said, the runtime can support a session-attach flow that attempts KV cache reuse for N seconds.

Notes / questions from runtime:
- We need a stable session identifier from the client (UUID) to map reconnect attempts to an existing KV cache. Is the SDK currently generating / surface such an id?
- If the token window/sequence diverges (client replay vs server state), we need a reconciliation policy we can document (e.g., prefer server-state and return a small 'resync' prefix).
- Short-term perf impact is small for a 10s reuse window, but we should test under concurrent session churn.

Dev — can you prototype a minimal session-attach handshake in the Go and Node SDKs today? If so, we can ship the sample snippet and runtime flag for Atria's test. I can help scope a quick canary plan.

Logan
Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ryan Chen <ryan@atrialabs.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify SDK reconnect semantics + demo stabilization plan

Logan / team —

I pulled the logs Tessa attached (atrialabs-demo-repro-logs.txt). Quick findings:
- The client reconnected with the same websocket session id twice after a short TCP reset. The runtime treated the second connection as a new session because there was no explicit session-attach token in the handshake. That led to two partial stream sequences being emitted to the client side.
- KV cache entries were still present on the worker for ~12s after disconnect (TTL default), so reuse should be possible if we attach.

Prototype plan (I can push a branch today):
1) SDK: Add optional header "X-Redwood-Session" (UUID) and a reconnect flag in the streaming handshake.
2) Runtime: If X-Redwood-Session matches an active KV cache and last activity < 15s, attempt attach and resume from last-ack token. If mismatch, return 409 with resync token suggestion.
3) Telemetry: Emit an event on attach success/failure and a short metric about reused vs new sessions.

Risks / follow-ups:
- Client must persist last-ack token and session id between reconnects; we'll document the snippet.
- Edge: mobile clients with NAT churn may have frequent reconnects; we should gate by a retry count.

I’ll open PRs for Node/Go SDKs and a runtime feature flag. ETA for a canary: 48 hours. I’ll attach the repro log snippets in the PR.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Ryan Chen <ryan@atrialabs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify SDK reconnect semantics + demo stabilization plan

Thanks all — this is great. Atria confirmed the client can persist the session UUID and last-ack token; we'll add that to the test harness today. Priorities for us: deterministic reconnect for the demo + clear failure semantics if resync is required.

Next actions we agreed on internally: 
- Dev will push SDK PRs and runtime branch (canary) — target 48h.
- Tessa / Marissa will send Atria the demo snippet and test matrix (load + flaky network).
- Logan to schedule a 30-min canary review once PRs are in.

If you want, Atria can also run an extended soak on the canary once it's available. We're comfortable with the 15s attach window you suggested.

Ryan
Lead POC Engineer, Atria Labs
